title: President Sheinbaum Says US Embassy & Chihuahua Government Must Explain Presence of US Agents in Mexico
author: Emir Olivares and Alonso Urrutia
content:
_This article by Emir Olivares and Alonso Urrutia originally appeared in
the[April 20, 2026 edition of
](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/04/20/politica/-embajada-y-gobierno-
de-chihuahua-deben-explicar-presencia-de-agentes-de-eu-en-operativo-contra-
narco-sheinbaum)_[La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/04/20/politica/-embajada-y-
gobierno-de-chihuahua-deben-explicar-presencia-de-agentes-de-eu-en-operativo-
contra-narco-sheinbaum) _, Mexico 's premier left wing daily newspaper._

Editor's note: [the _Washington Post_ is reporting as of the morning of April
21, 2026 that the two agents were CIA
officers](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/04/21/cia-
mexico-accident-counter-narcotics).

**Mexico City**. President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo emphasized that information
will be requested from both the United States government and the Chihuahua
state government regarding the presence of two U.S. security agents in field
operations to determine if any laws were violated.

This, she emphasized, is because the regulations stipulate that the presence
in Mexican territory of elements from the agencies of the northern neighbor
must be regulated, comply with protocols and must be authorized by the
Federation.

“The relationship is federal, not state. They need authorization from the
Federation for this collaboration that takes place at the state level, as
established by the Constitution.”

The President was questioned about whether she knew about the activities
carried out by two agents from Washington, after their presence in the country
became known due to an accident in which they lost their lives yesterday along
with two members of the Chihuahua State Investigation Agency, when they were
returning from an operation to dismantle drug laboratories.

“We weren't aware of it; it was a decision made by the Chihuahua state
government (under Governor Maru Campos). We are requesting more information
from the Chihuahua government. Regardless of the situation, we regret this
accident. They have the full solidarity and support of the Mexican government,
and we are in contact with the U.S. Embassy. Secondly, we were unaware of any
direct collaboration between Chihuahua and personnel from the U.S. Embassy in
Mexico.”

The head of the Executive Branch insisted that "all the information" has been
requested from both the state administration and the United States embassy,
​​in order to review whether the law on the matter was violated by that
agreement at the level of an entity of the Republic.

“It is important, not only, we are clear on this, we have stated it this way,
that there is collaboration, there is coordination, but there are no joint
operations on the ground. There is information that is provided from them to
us and from us to them, intelligence, we collaborate within this framework. We
also appreciate the support in this regard within the framework of our
sovereignty, with the four principles that we have established regarding the
territorial integrity of Mexico.”

The federal leader insisted that as soon as her government has the
information, it will be made public.

"The embassy has to give us the information, and of course, we will provide as
much information as possible, without affecting the safety of people and
within the framework of security measures."

She mentioned that she herself, if she has the opportunity, will demand
answers this Monday from the US ambassador, Ronald Johnson, who will be
attending the meeting this morning with the US trade representative.
